Subject: Post-call recap & follow-ups: reserved capacity sizing / target $/1M

Thanks again for taking the time today — concise recap and a few asks so we can turn this into a scoped reserved-capacity proposal. High level takeaway from the call: Crestline is looking for a dedicated inference lane for generative insights (long-context summarization + question answering) with strong latency requirements and predictable unit economics.

Key notes from call:
- Expected steady-state monthly consumption: ~350M tokens (combined embed + gen) — please confirm if this aggregates all environments (prod+staging).
- Peak traffic: ~4.5k concurrent users roughly translating to 1.6k tokens/sec at 95th pct (ballpark from the demo).
- Latency SLO: 150ms p50 for short queries, 300ms p95 for long-context ops (this was called out as a must-have).
- Preference: interested in H100 for highest perf but open to A100 80GB if price delta is significant.
- Target unit economics (your comment): target budget of $150–$190 per 1M tokens for reserved capacity (target $/1M: please confirm a hard cap).

Action items (from Redwood):
1) Ben to produce two preliminary SKUs (H100-focused and an A100-quantized variant) with estimated throughput per-GPU, assumed prompt lengths, and estimated $/1M tokens. Deliverable: ballpark CSV + assumptions.
2) Crestline to confirm: total monthly token volume (350M is our working number), % of generation vs embedding, expected 95th percentile concurrency window (15m vs 5m), and any hard budget cap.
3) Review PoC plan and sample SOW items to support a 60-day reserved trial (if Crestline wants that).

Attachments: reserved-estimate-template.xlsx (filled partially during call).

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up to go through the two SKUs and pick a PoC target (time options: Tue 7/7 10–11am PT or Wed 7/8 2–3pm PT).

Thanks — I'll pull Ben's hypotheses together by EOD tomorrow.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Initial sizing + two-ballpark SKUs (assumptions included)

Samira — good notes. I ran a quick hypothesis pass (attached) and sketched two conservative SKUs based on the numbers you provided. Put the assumptions up front so procurement has transparency.

Assumptions (high level):
- Effective token mix: 70% gen / 30% embed, avg gen output 120 tokens, prompt 60 tokens.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching expected to reduce repeated-context cost by ~12% (depends on workload).
- Duty cycle / utilization: for reserved lanes we assume ~65% average GPU utilization to preserve headroom and p95 SLOs.
- Billing model: committed reserved capacity billed monthly + metered token overage at market rate; we can propose a capped burst rate (pre-agreed) during PoC.

SKU 1 — H100 reserved lane (preferred)
- Initial commit: 8 x H100 (reserved)
- Estimated steady throughput: ~2.2k tokens/sec sustained across the pool (95th window), headroom for 2.8k bursts.
- Estimated unit cost: $165 / 1M tokens (committed volume at 380M/mo).
- Monthly committed spend estimate: ~ $62,700 (range $58k–$68k depending on actual utilization/efficiency).

SKU 2 — A100-optimized (quantized, cost-first)
- Initial commit: 12 x A100 80GB (reserved, quantized weights)
- Estimated steady throughput: ~1.8k tokens/sec sustained, burst to ~2.6k tokens/sec with elastic lanes.
- Estimated unit cost: $125 / 1M tokens (committed volume at 380M/mo).
- Monthly committed spend estimate: ~ $47,500 (range $44k–$51k).

Notes / tradeoffs:
- H100 brings lower p95 latency and simpler accuracy profile; A100 requires more aggressive quantization and may increase failure modes for some long-context ops.
- We recommend starting with H100 for the critical production lane and running an A100 quantized lane for lower-cost bulk embedding workloads if you want to mix.

Attachments: ballpark_pricing_hypotheses.csv (contains per-GPU throughput assumptions, token-to-cost math, and sensitivity to prompt length).

Questions for Crestline before the Wed 7/8 meeting:
- Confirm whether staging traffic will be part of the reserved commit or handled separately.
- Any mandatory encryption/KMS requirements (HSM)? The PoC checklist attached by Samira flagged this.
- Acceptable overage policy: do you want automatic burst billing up to X% or throttling after the reserved capacity is exhausted?

I can present the SKU slides in Wed's call. If procurement wants an SOW/60-day trial clause we can draft a short MSA addendum + trial SOW.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
